name: Executive Order of May 15, 1876 correctly defining the boundaries of the Colorado River reservation (Royce area 593)
nations: Colorado River Indian Tribes (Mohave, Chemehuevi, Hopi and Navajo)
promises: An enlargement, not a cession: the President, referring to previous errors, defined the boundaries of the reservation established by the Act of March 3, 1865 and enlarged in 1873 and 1874, from La Paz arroyo to Black Mountain, across the river to Monument Peak and Riverside Mountain in California, and back along the west bank (Royce pp. 886-887).
Royce records that the order of November 16, 1874 had defective boundaries and was superseded by this one (Royce p. 877).
landTaken: None by this order; it added land. The Indian Claims Commission dated the taking of Mohave lands outside the reservation to the Act of March 3, 1865 (Dockets 283 and 295), which is the separate record cession-1865-03-03-colorado-river.
today: The Colorado River Indian Tribes say the reservation, created in 1865, stretches along both banks of the river and includes almost 300,000 acres.

nationVoice.summary: CRIT says the reservation was created in 1865 for the Indians of the Colorado River, first the Mohave and Chemehuevi who had lived there for centuries, with Hopi and Navajo people relocated there later.

openQuestions: The dispute over the reservation's western (California) boundary under this order, litigated in Arizona v. California, was not researched; whether any ruling treats land inside these boundaries as taken was not checked.
The Mohave decision (id 283) was relied on as cited in cession-1874-11-16-colorado-river and was not re-read in full for this file.
